q: How do a man and woman become one flesh?
a: The man will unite to the woman as his wife.

q: Were the man and his wife ashamed of being naked?
a: No.

q: What was the name of Abram’s wife?
a: Abram’s wife’s name was Sarai.

q: What problem did Abram’s wife have?
a: Abram’s wife’s Sarai was barren; she had no children.

q: What was Abram concerned about as he entered Egypt?
a: Abram was concerned the Egyptians would kill him and take his wife Sarai, because she was beautiful.

q: What question did Pharaoh ask Abram?
a: Pharaoh asked Abram why he had told him that Sarai was his sister instead of his wife.

q: How did Abram respond to Yahweh’s promise, and what did Yahweh then do?
a: Abram believed Yahweh, and Yahweh counted it to Abram as righteousness.

q: What did Yahweh say Abraham must do so that Yahweh might fulfill the promises given to Abraham?
a: Yahweh said that Abraham must instruct his children and his household to do righteousness and justice.

q: What did Isaac do after Abraham’s servant recounted all the things that he had done?
a: Isaac brought Rebekah into his mother Sarah’s tent and took Rebekah as his wife.

q: What did Isaac do because Rebekah was childless?
a: Isaac prayed to Yahweh for his wife; Yahweh answered his prayer, and Rebekah conceived.

q: What did Isaac say to the men of Gerar about Rebekah, his wife?
a: Isaac told the men of Gerar that Rebekah was his sister.

q: What command did Isaac give Jacob before he left?
a: Isaac commanded Jacob not to take a Canaanite wife.

q: Why did Laban say he had tricked Jacob?
a: Laban said it was not their custom to give the younger daughter in marriage before the firstborn.

q: What did Hamor, the father of Shechem, want Jacob to do?
a: Hamor wanted Jacob to give Dinah to Shechem as his wife, and to allow Jacob’s family to intermarry with Hamor’s family.

q: What did Shechem say he was willing to do to have Dinah as his wife?
a: Shechem said he would pay as great a bride price as Jacob would name.

q: From whom did Judah take a wife?
a: Judah took a wife who was a daughter of a Canaanite man.

q: What promise did Judah then make to Tamar?
a: Judah promised Tamar his third son, Shelah, as a husband when Shelah grew up.

q: After a long time, why did Judah need to be comforted?
a: Judah needed to be comforted because his wife had died.

q: Why did Tamar do this?
a: Tamar did this because Judah’s third son Shelah had grown up, but she had not been given to him as a wife.

q: What did Potiphar’s wife ask Joseph to do?
a: Potiphar’s wife asked Joseph to lie with her.

q: How did Joseph respond to Potiphar’s wife’s request?
a: Joseph refused and said he could not commit this great evil and sin against God.

q: What accusation did Potiphar’s wife make against Joseph?
a: She accused him of trying to lie with her against her will.

q: What message did Joseph hear about his father, and what did he then do?
a: Joseph heard that his father was sick, so he took with him his two sons.

q: What promises from God did Jacob recall to Joseph?
a: Jacob recalled that God promised him that he would be fruitful and multiply, he would be made a community of peoples, and the land of Canaan would be an everlasting possession of his offspring.
